annotations.text:
A · Sketch grid — the attached sketch, literally.
Two by two at every width, screenshots tilted and broken out of the card top. Reads as a toy shelf.
Tradeoff: at 390px the two-up cards leave ~150px of text width, so the blurbs have to be short — that is the least SEO copy of the three.

B · Marquee row — four abreast, editorial hero.
Left-aligned hero so the h1 and the paragraph read as one block; cards straight-on and equal weight.
Tradeoff: four equal cards say all four tools are equally real. Three of them are not.

C · Featured — the shipped tool leads.
The dex builder gets a split hero card with a real screenshot and a solid CTA; the other three sit in a supporting row.
Tradeoff: it buries the league builder, which is the tool with a settled spec and the next page to rank.

SEO structure, same in all three:
· h1 carries "make your own Pokédex" plus region and league.
· Each card is an <h2> that exactly matches its slug: /custom-pokedex-builder, /custom-gym-leader, /favorite-pokemon-picker.
· The footer repeats the four links as anchor text.
Watch out: making / a router moves the dex builder off the URL that ranks today (~pos 7.8 for "pokedex builder").

D · Poster cards. Mobile and tablet space out evenly: three equal flex spacers put the same gap above the intro text, between the text and the grid, and between the grid and the footer.
The Hammer is centred between the card's top edge and the top of its heading, so the space above it matches the space below by construction rather than by eye.
Desktop has about 110px between the sub-text and the artwork, which is the room for a hover nudge.

Responsive check — `node docs/future-tools/home-page/sweep.mjs`.
The layout is a function of width: `posterConfig(width, height)`. Two regimes meet at 1024, the app's own md breakpoint — stacked hero and two cards up below it, split hero and four across at and above it. Inside a regime every number is piecewise-linear between anchors, and the anchors are the shipped page's own numbers.
The sweep drives 45 frames from 320 to 2560 in Chromium and reads geometry, not text: horizontal overflow, the footer sitting below the fold, hero/grid/footer band order, card-on-card overlap, one-line headings, blurb clipping, a bare red strip at every card's right edge, artwork landing on the card above, and the mark centred in its card. 45 of 45 are clean.
`--mutate all` injects seven known defects and asserts each is caught. A sweep that cannot fail is not evidence.
The fold now fits a short phone: it needs 595px at 390 wide, 942px at 834, and 490px at 1440.

These artboards are taller than the viewport on purpose. The header, hero and card grid fill one screen on their own; the footer starts below that fold. What a visitor sees before scrolling is everything down to the footer's top rule — the rest is a scroll away.
Inside the fold, three equal spacers put the same air above the hero, between the hero and the grid, and below the grid.
The card: the screenshot shadow fades out over its last 34px instead of stopping in a straight line at the card's bottom edge; the screenshots themselves still cut on that edge, which is what makes them read as sliding behind the card.
Card copy is 9.4px title and 8.8px blurb at 390. It cannot reach the 11.5px of the "No account…" line: "Trainer Card & League Builder" already fills 154 of the 158px the card gives it, so one line of title caps the size at about 9.6px.
The h1 is 21px on a phone — the largest whole pixel that keeps it to two lines at 320px. Line breaks come from `text-wrap: pretty` on the hero and `balance` in the cards, never manual breaks.
